# Min Cost Climbing Stairs.

@example Start on pad 0, pay 4 to land on pad 2, then pay 3 to launch from it to the finish.
[4,9,3,7]
=> 7

@example Start on pad 1, so pad 0's 8 is never paid: 2 takes you to pad 3, and 1 from there to the finish.
[8,2,6,1,5]
=> 3

@example Launch from pads 1, 2 and 4, paying 1 + 1 + 4. Going from pad 1 to the very next pad lets the route use both cheap pads.
[5,1,1,6,4]
=> 6

# The fewest pads: start on pad 1 and leave it for the finish.
[12,3]
=> 3

# Three pads: pad 0 can't reach the finish, so pad 2 is paid too. The
# answer is larger than 255.
[260,990,300]
=> 560

# The cheapest route skips the last pad, launching from pad 2 over it.
[4,6,2,9]
=> 6

# Taking the cheaper of the next two pads each time pays 1 + 2 + 1 = 4;
# starting on pad 1 pays 2 + 1.
[1,2,10,1,10]
=> 3

# A free route through pads 1, 2 and 4, which no route that always skips
# a pad can take.
[8,0,0,8,0]
=> 0

# Nothing to pay.
[0,0,0]
=> 0

# All fees equal: pads 1, 3, 5, ... are paid, for odd and even n.
[7,7,7,7,7,7,7]
=> 21

[7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7]
=> 28

# Rising and falling fees.
[2,4,6,8,10,12,14]
=> 24

[90,70,50,30,10]
=> 100
